trophies.guide: The platinum. It pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do. Use the tracker: when the counter reads 54 / 55, the one left is your next job, and the roadmap order tells you the cheapest way to close it. Most players finish on a collectible sweep or the 100% checklist, so leave a short one for last.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.t: Open the tracker and mark every trophy you have already earned; the counter shows what is left.
Work the roadmap in order, cheapest unearned trophy first, so nothing expensive is left for the end.
Sweep collectibles by region in stage 5 — meditations, cards, WAiNK spots and vehicles are the usual last ones.
Finish the crime trophies in stage 6, then the final mission in stage 7.
Complete the 100% checklist for A Long Road; the platinum unlocks with the final trophy.
If the platinum does not pop, re-check the tracker: one trophy is still unmarked or uncounted.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing the Chapter 1 mission Gone Fishing. It is unmissable: play the story and it unlocks at the mission's end. Use it as the moment to start the fishing counter — beating Cal in a fishing challenge later needs the same water, so learn the cast here.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps.t: Play Chapter 1 until the mission Gone Fishing appears in the story flow.
Follow the mission markers to the fishing spot and complete the fishing sequence.
Finish the mission's closing scene; the trophy pops at the end of the mission.
After it pops, try a free fishing challenge nearby — it teaches the cast you need for Baited My Tackle.
The trophy cannot be missed: replaying the mission from the chapter select also unlocks it.
Mark it earned in the tracker to keep the Chapter 1 group honest.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 1. It unlocks automatically when the last Chapter 1 mission ends. Before you leave Chapter 1, do the one thing that may not come back: the balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude, which several guides warn can end with the chapter.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

steps.t: Play through every Chapter 1 story mission in order.
Before the final Chapter 1 mission, do the balcony meditation at Jason's house for Positive Mental Attitude.
Finish the chapter's closing mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card.
Check the tracker: Chapter 1 group should read complete except any collectibles you are saving for later.
If a Chapter 1 mission was skipped, replay it from chapter select — the trophy still unlocks.
Move on to Chapter 2; nothing in Chapter 1 stays locked except the balcony meditation.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 2. It unlocks when the last Chapter 2 mission ends. Chapter 2 opens the partner swap between Lucia and Jason — use it to double up on the meditation spots, since meditating with both leads at a marked spot counts twice toward Positive Mental Attitude.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps.t: Start Chapter 2 from the story flow after Chapter 1 ends.
Play every Chapter 2 mission in order; side content can wait.
When the partner unlock lands, meditate at any marked spot with both leads to bank two counts at once.
Finish the chapter's closing mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card.
Check the Chapter 2 group in the tracker before moving on.
Missed a mission? Chapter select replays it and the trophy still unlocks.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 3. It unlocks at the end of the chapter's last mission. Chapter 3 is where the map opens up — good moment to start the vehicle count for Whip It Good, since new districts bring new traffic.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

steps.t: Play Chapter 3 from the story flow.
Complete each Chapter 3 mission in order.
Between missions, steal and drive new vehicles to start the 100-vehicle count.
Finish the closing mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card.
Check the tracker: the Chapter 3 group should be complete.
Replay any skipped mission from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 4. It unlocks at the end of the chapter's last mission. By now the stranger strands are open — start them before the finale, because several of their final missions are the ones the roadmap flags as watch-listed.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

steps.t: Play Chapter 4 from the story flow.
Complete each Chapter 4 mission in order.
Between missions, pick up the first stranger strands so their chains are running.
Finish the closing mission; the trophy pops at the chapter card.
Check the tracker: the Chapter 4 group should be complete.
Replay any skipped mission from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Gold story trophy for completing the final mission. It unlocks at the end of the finale. Do it last in the story order but not necessarily last overall — the collectible and activity sweeps are easier after the finale, when the whole map is open and nothing is chapter-locked anymore.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

steps.t: Finish Chapters 1–4 and the stranger strands you want done before the finale.
Start the final mission from the story flow.
Play the finale to its end; the trophy pops at the closing scene.
After it pops, the whole map is open — the best time for the collectible sweeps.
Check the tracker: only activities, collectibles and 100% should remain.
The finale can be replayed from chapter select if anything went wrong.

dispute.a: Yes — it is a one-time set-piece: rush past the opening and the mission window closes. [20]
dispute.b: No — it is a story mission, so it always appears when you follow the story. [1] [14]
dispute.call: Same move either way: follow the story markers in Chapter 1 and do it the first time it appears.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Breakfast Run. It is a story mission, so it cannot be missed outright — but guides flag it at risk because it is a one-time set-piece early in Chapter 1: if you rush past the opening hours without following the story markers, you can be several hours in before it appears. Follow the story and it pops.
trophies.name: Trust

steps.t: Play Chapter 1 and follow the story markers; Breakfast Run appears early in the chapter.
Do not wander off into free roam for long stretches before the mission appears.
Start Breakfast Run from the marker and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If you have passed the opening hours and it has not appeared, check the story log — you may have missed a marker.
Replay from chapter select if needed; the trophy still unlocks.

dispute.a: Yes — rushing Chapter 2 skips a setup and the heist never triggers. [20] [27]
dispute.b: No — the setups are story-gated and always appear in order. [1] [14]
dispute.call: Do every setup the moment it appears; it costs minutes and removes the doubt.
dispute.q: Can the heist setups be skipped?

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission The Cartel Heist. It is a story mission, so it always appears — the at-risk flag is there because guides disagree about whether its setup steps can be skipped by rushing the chapter. Do the setups when they appear and the heist follows.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

steps.t: Play Chapter 2 until The Cartel Heist appears in the story flow.
Complete the heist setup steps when they appear; do not skip them.
Start the heist and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the heist completes.
If the heist has not appeared, check the story log for an unplayed setup mission.
Replay from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Child's Play. It is a story mission and appears in the Chapter 1 flow. Guides flag it at risk for the same reason as the other early set-pieces: rush the opening and you can be hours in before it shows. Follow the story markers and it pops.
trophies.name: Family Matters

steps.t: Play Chapter 1 and follow the story markers; Child's Play appears early.
Do not spend long in free roam before the mission appears.
Start Child's Play from the marker and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If it has not appeared, check the story log for an unplayed marker.
Replay from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Headliners. It is a story mission in the Chapter 2 flow. The at-risk flag is there because it is a one-time set-piece: guides disagree about whether it can be replayed cleanly if you fail its opening, so play it the first time it appears and do not rush its setup.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

steps.t: Play Chapter 2 until Headliners appears in the story flow.
Do the setup steps when they appear; do not skip them.
Start Headliners and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If it has not appeared, check the story log for an unplayed setup.
Replay from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission VCIA Takedown. It is a story mission in the Chapter 2 flow. Like the other one-time set-pieces it is flagged at risk: several guides warn that rushing the chapter can leave its setup unplayed for hours. Follow the markers and it pops.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

steps.t: Play Chapter 2 until VCIA Takedown appears in the story flow.
Complete its setup steps when they appear.
Start VCIA Takedown and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If it has not appeared, check the story log for an unplayed setup.
Replay from chapter select if needed.

trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Operation Savage Glory. It is a story mission in the Chapter 2 flow. Guides flag it at risk because it is a late-chapter set-piece with a long setup chain — skip the chain and the mission stays locked. Do the setups in order and it pops.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

steps.t: Play Chapter 2 until Operation Savage Glory appears in the story flow.
Complete the setup chain in order; skipping a setup delays the mission.
Start the operation and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If it has not appeared, check the story log for an unplayed setup.
Replay from chapter select if needed.

dispute.a: Yes — every checklist item counts: story, activities, collectibles and counts. [3] [16]
dispute.b: No — only the story, activities and the counted challenges count; some collectibles are optional. [1] [27]
dispute.call: Treat every checklist item as required; it is the safe play and it is how the in-game percentage reads.

trophies.guide: Gold trophy for attaining 100% completion. The in-game checklist (Progress > Collections > Completion) is the source of truth: story missions, activities, collectible sets and the counted challenges all feed the percentage. Work it last, after the finale, when nothing is chapter-locked — and use the tracker, because the percentage is the only number that matters here.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps.t: Finish the story, including the final mission, before chasing the percentage.
Open Progress > Collections > Completion and note which rows are incomplete.
Clear the activity rows first: shooting range golds, 250 stunts, drone races, 20 race wins.
Sweep the collectible rows by region: meditations, cards, WAiNK spots, vehicles.
Finish the counted rows: 50 challenges, 3 card sets, 100 vehicles, 100 WAiNK spots.
When the percentage reads 100%, the trophy pops; if it does not, one row is still short.
Re-check the row the tracker flags — the in-game list is the authority, not this guide.

dispute.a: Yes — stunts by either lead count toward the same total. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — only the lead who performs the stunt banks it, so split them carefully. [5] [16]
dispute.call: Play both leads and watch the counter; it climbs either way in practice.
dispute.q: Do stunts count across both leads?

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and drift chains the game scores in free roam — the counter is in Progress > Collections. The fastest route is a loop of the big ramps and long jumps with a fast bike, chaining airtime into drifts; do it in batches between story missions so it never feels like a grind.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps.t: Open Progress > Collections and find the stunt counter to see your starting number.
Take a fast bike to a long ramp or jump and build airtime, then chain a drift on landing.
Near-misses in traffic and long drifts count too — mix them into the same runs.
Work in batches of 25–50 between story missions rather than in one sitting.
Use both leads; the counter climbs for the account, not per character.
Watch the counter after each batch; at 250 the trophy pops.
If the counter stalls, vary the stunt type — repeating one jump scores less over time.

trophies.desc: Try each type of activity once.

dispute.a: Yes — every activity type in the game counts, including the ones the map never labels. [16] [27]
dispute.b: No — only the labelled activities in the Activities menu count. [1] [3]
dispute.call: Open the Activities menu and clear every labelled type first; the hidden ones surface there too.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for trying each type of activity once. The Activities menu (Progress > Activities) lists the types: shooting range, drone races, races, fishing, arcade, bowling, meditation and more. One attempt at each is enough — you do not need to win or finish anything, just try it.
trophies.name: Master of None

steps.t: Open Progress > Activities and list every activity type shown.
Try the shooting range once, any challenge.
Try a drone race, a road race, a fishing challenge and an arcade game.
Try bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley and a meditation at any spot.
Try any remaining type the menu lists — one attempt each is enough.
The trophy pops when the last type is tried; the menu shows what is left.
If one type will not tick, re-open the menu — some types only appear after the partner unlock.

trophies.desc: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.

dispute.a: Yes — all 42 challenges need gold, every weapon class. [4] [16]
dispute.b: No — only the challenges the range lists when you first arrive count. [1] [27]
dispute.call: Gold every challenge the range shows; the counter reads 42 when you are done.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for earning a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. The range lists every challenge by weapon class with its gold threshold — the thresholds are shown before you start, so pick the easiest weapon class first and learn the recoil pattern. Gold is about clean, steady shooting, not speed: take the time bonus slowly and keep your grouping tight.
trophies.name: The Shootist

steps.t: Visit any shooting range and open the challenge list; it shows all 42 challenges.
Start with the easiest weapon class and learn its gold threshold and recoil.
Aim for grouping, not speed — gold rewards clean hits over fast misses.
Work through the weapon classes one at a time and mark golds in the tracker.
For the hard classes, use the range's practice mode first to learn the pattern.
When all 42 show gold, the trophy pops.
If a challenge will not turn gold, check its threshold — some need a perfect run, not just a pass.

trophies.desc: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.

dispute.a: Yes — every location on the map has a drone race, and all of them count. [12] [16]
dispute.b: No — only the locations the Top Fun menu lists count. [1] [13]
dispute.call: Win every race the Top Fun menu lists; that is the full set the game tracks.
dispute.q: How many drone race locations are there?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for winning a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. The Top Fun menu lists the race locations; each one is a short drone course through rings. Learn the course with a practice run first — the winning line is usually the low line through the rings, not the fast line over them.
trophies.name: Top Fun

steps.t: Open the Top Fun menu and list every drone race location.
Start with the shortest course and fly a practice run to learn the rings.
Race the low line through the rings; it is faster than the high line.
Win each location once and mark it in the tracker.
Work through the locations in order; the menu shows which are won.
When every location shows a win, the trophy pops.
If a location will not tick, re-check the menu — a race only counts on a full win, not a practice run.

dispute.a: Yes — any 20 different race events count, road or off-road. [13] [16]
dispute.b: No — only the 20 races in the official race series count. [1] [13]
dispute.call: Win the races the race menu lists; the counter shows the total as you go.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for winning 20 different races. The race menu lists the road and off-road events across Leonida; each event counts once when you win it. Pick the short circuits first and learn their corners — a clean line beats a fast car on most of them.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

steps.t: Open the race menu and list the events across Leonida.
Start with the short circuits and learn their corners.
Win each event once; the counter climbs per event, not per win.
Mix road and off-road events so the count keeps moving.
Use the fastest car you own for the long events and a nimble one for the tight ones.
At 20 different wins the trophy pops.
If the counter stalls, check the menu — a repeat win of the same event does not count.

trophies.desc: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.

dispute.a: Yes — Cal only appears at one spot, at dawn, with the right bait. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — Cal roams the fishing spots and any challenge win against him counts. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Challenge Cal wherever he appears; the win is what counts, not the spot.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for beating Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival who appears at the challenge spots — challenge him, then fish the way the challenge asks: steady reeling, no slack, and watch the line tension. The first win is the hardest; after that the pattern repeats.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

steps.t: Find a fishing challenge spot and look for Cal's marker.
Start the challenge and note what it asks: biggest catch, most fish, or fastest time.
Reel steadily and keep the line tension in the safe zone.
Beat Cal's score once; the trophy pops on the win.
If you lose, retry at once — the challenge resets and Cal stays.
Try a different spot if Cal never appears; he rotates between them.
Use the bait the challenge suggests — it changes which fish bite.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing an arcade game. Any arcade cabinet in Leonida counts — pick one, play it to its end, and the trophy pops. The arcade games are short: most take a few minutes, and none of them need a high score, just a completion.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

steps.t: Find an arcade cabinet in Leonida — bars and arcades have them.
Pick any game and start it.
Play the game to its end; a high score is not needed, only a completion.
The trophy pops when the game ends.
If the cabinet is busy, try another one — any cabinet counts.
The shortest games are the best first pick if you only want the trophy.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Andy.

dispute.a: Yes — Andy's chain must be finished before the finale, or it locks. [16] [20]
dispute.b: No — the chain stays open after the finale and can be finished later. [1] [14]
dispute.call: Finish Andy's chain before the finale; it costs one session and removes the doubt.
dispute.q: Must Andy's chain end before the finale?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing the final mission for Andy. Andy's stranger chain runs through several missions; the last one is the trophy. The chain is watch-listed because guides disagree about whether it stays open after the finale — finish it before the finale and the question never matters.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

steps.t: Find Andy's first stranger mission and start the chain.
Play each mission in the chain in order; new ones appear after each.
Do the chain before the finale — that is the safe play.
Start the final mission for Andy and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If a mission has not appeared, check the map for Andy's marker.
The chain can be replayed from the mission log if needed.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing the final mission for Kenton. Kenton's stranger chain runs through several missions; the last one is the trophy. Like the other stranger chains it is watch-listed: finish it before the finale so nothing is left to chance.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

steps.t: Find Kenton's first stranger mission and start the chain.
Play each mission in the chain in order.
Do the chain before the finale — that is the safe play.
Start the final mission for Kenton and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If a mission has not appeared, check the map for Kenton's marker.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Billy.

dispute.a: Yes — Billy's last mission only appears in one chapter window. [16] [20]
dispute.b: No — the chain is open until the finale and the last mission always appears. [1] [14]
dispute.call: Finish Billy's chain before the finale; it costs one session and removes the doubt.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing the final mission for Billy. Billy's stranger chain runs through several missions; the last one is the trophy. It is watch-listed for the same reason as the other chains: guides disagree about its window, so finish it before the finale.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

steps.t: Find Billy's first stranger mission and start the chain.
Play each mission in the chain in order.
Do the chain before the finale — that is the safe play.
Start the final mission for Billy and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If a mission has not appeared, check the map for Billy's marker.
The chain can be replayed from the mission log if needed.

trophies.desc: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.

dispute.a: Yes — any 8 completed strands count, including the short ones. [16] [27]
dispute.b: No — only the 8 named stranger chains count; short encounters do not. [1] [3]
dispute.call: Complete the named chains; the counter shows the total as you go.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Stranger missions appear as question marks on the map; each chain is a strand. Work them as they appear — the map shows new ones after each chapter — and the counter in Progress > Collections tracks the total.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

steps.t: Open the map and note the stranger markers across Leonida.
Start the nearest strand and play its missions in order.
Work the strands as they appear after each chapter.
Finish each strand's final mission; the counter climbs per strand.
Keep going until 8 strands are complete.
At 8 the trophy pops.
If the counter stalls, check the map — a strand only counts when its final mission is done.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Randy.

dispute.a: Yes — Randy's chain closes at the finale like the others. [16] [20]
dispute.b: No — Randy's chain stays open after the finale. [1] [14]
dispute.call: Finish Randy's chain before the finale; it costs one session and removes the doubt.
dispute.q: Does Randy's chain close at the finale?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing the final mission for Randy. Randy's stranger chain runs through several missions; the last one is the trophy. It is watch-listed like the other chains: finish it before the finale and the question never matters.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

steps.t: Find Randy's first stranger mission and start the chain.
Play each mission in the chain in order.
Do the chain before the finale — that is the safe play.
Start the final mission for Randy and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If a mission has not appeared, check the map for Randy's marker.
The chain can be replayed from the mission log if needed.

trophies.desc: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone's stranger chain runs through several missions; the last one is the trophy. Like the other chains it is watch-listed: finish it before the finale so nothing is left to chance.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

steps.t: Find Tyrone's first stranger mission and start the chain.
Play each mission in the chain in order.
Do the chain before the finale — that is the safe play.
Start the final mission for Tyrone and play it to the end.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
If a mission has not appeared, check the map for Tyrone's marker.

trophies.desc: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.

dispute.a: Yes — the balcony counts: it raises the counter by 1, and the trophy needs every spot. [2] [13]
dispute.b: Unproven — the balcony is not marked as a standard spot, and the final meditation may count double so the total still reaches 18 without it. [1] [2] [17]
dispute.call: Same move either way: do the balcony meditation in Chapter 1. It costs two minutes and covers every reading; skipping it is a gamble on an unconfirmed theory.

trophies.guide: The one trophy this guide flags as possibly missable. Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 in total, because meditating with both leads at a marked spot counts twice. The first meditation is the Chapter 1 balcony at Jason's house: follow Lucia to the balcony in the morning after Down to Earth. Several guides warn the balcony spot ends with Chapter 1, and whether the trophy needs it is unconfirmed — so do it in Chapter 1 and the question never matters.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

steps.t: Chapter 1: the morning after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house.
Follow her to the balcony and accept the meditation; it adds to the counter although it is not a marked spot. [5] [25] [27]
Keep the Chapter 1 manual save until the trophy pops. [2] [14] [24]
Spots 2–9 count once for Jason and once for Lucia, so bring your partner. [5] [25] [27]

Open-world spots: Smooth Sand (sandbar west of Capri), Swamp (Buckskin Swamp dock), Worn Stone (Camp Moonflower), Red Rocks (Manifest Canyon), Water Wheel (paper mill south of Moreau), Jutting Cliff (Mount Kalaga National Park), Waterfall (north-west Tallalooka) and Seaside (east of Waning Sands). [5] [32]
Ascent Mountain, the stone circle on Mount Kalaga's peak, only appears once the others are done and needs both characters, so it waits for Coffee Break. [3] [2] [37] [41]
Watch the counter under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations; 100% only asks for 15 of 18, the trophy needs all 18. [35] [2] [37] [41] [4]

trophies.desc: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.

dispute.a: Yes — the animal only appears at one den, at dawn. [11] [16]
dispute.b: No — unique animals roam and any hunt of the named one counts. [1] [11]
dispute.call: Go to the den at dawn; that is where every guide agrees the animal is.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for hunting a unique animal for Bret. Bret's stranger chain points you at a single named animal — the unique ones have their own dens and habits. Go to the den at dawn, track it quietly, and take the shot when it is still. A loud approach scares it off and costs you the trip.
trophies.name: Fair Game

steps.t: Find Bret's stranger mission and start the chain.
Follow the chain until Bret names the unique animal and its den.
Go to the den at dawn, when the animal is out.
Approach quietly and take the shot while it is still.
Return the animal to Bret to finish the hunt.
The trophy pops when the hunt completes.
If the animal is not there, leave the area and come back at dawn — it respawns on the same schedule.

dispute.a: Yes — a set only counts when every card in it is found. [8] [16]
dispute.b: No — the sets complete when the last card of any set is found, even mid-set. [1] [8]
dispute.call: Finish sets one at a time; the tracker shows each set's progress.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 3 Collectible Card sets. The cards are scattered across Leonida in fixed spots — shops, bars, hideouts and the open world. Work one set at a time by region so you never backtrack, and use the tracker: each set shows how many cards are left.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

steps.t: Open Progress > Collections and see the three card sets and their counts.
Pick one set and sweep its region for the cards, using the map markers.
Check cards off in the tracker as you find them.
Finish the first set completely before starting the second.
Sweep the second and third sets the same way.
When the third set completes, the trophy pops.
If a card will not appear, re-check the set list — some cards only spawn after a story beat.

dispute.a: Yes — only the 100 marked WAiNK spots count. [7] [16]
dispute.b: No — any 100 photos of named locations count. [1] [7]
dispute.call: Photograph the marked spots; the counter shows the total as you go.

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for using WAiNK at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game photo app: open it at a named location, frame the shot, and it logs the spot. The 100 spots are spread across Leonida — work them region by region and let the tracker count them, so you never photograph the same spot twice.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps.t: Open the WAiNK app and see the location list and your count.
Pick a region and photograph its marked spots one by one.
Frame the named location in the shot; the app logs it when the name appears.
Work region by region and mark spots in the tracker.
Keep going until the counter reads 100.
At 100 the trophy pops.
If a spot will not log, re-frame it — the location name must be visible in the shot.

dispute.a: Yes — only the 50 challenges in the Challenges menu count. [1] [16]
dispute.b: No — any 50 completed challenges count, including repeatable ones. [3] [27]
dispute.call: Work the Challenges menu; the counter shows the total as you go.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for completing 50 challenges. The Challenges menu (Progress > Challenges) lists them by type — driving, shooting, flying, exploration and more. Pick the short ones first and batch them by region; the counter climbs per challenge, and the menu shows exactly which are done.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

steps.t: Open Progress > Challenges and list what is available.
Start with the shortest challenges — the driving and exploration ones are quick.
Batch challenges by region so travel is never wasted.
Work through the list and mark completions in the tracker.
Keep going until the counter reads 50.
At 50 the trophy pops.
If the counter stalls, re-open the menu — some challenges only appear after story beats.

trophies.desc: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.

dispute.a: Yes — the escape only counts if your partner is with you the whole chase. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — the trophy pops as long as the wanted level is lost while partnered. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Keep your partner beside you until the stars clear; that satisfies both readings.
dispute.q: Must your partner stay through the whole escape?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for losing a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escaping the heat. Get the law to 4 stars with your partner in the car, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. It is flagged at risk because it is a one-time-feeling set-piece — in practice it can be repeated, but do it early, while the partner missions are running, so the setup is natural.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps.t: Wait until a partner mission has your partner in the car with you.
Raise the wanted level to 4 stars — a crime spree in a busy district does it fast.
Break line of sight: lose the helicopters first, then the ground units.
Stay hidden until all four stars clear.
The trophy pops when the stars clear with your partner still with you.
If the stars drop to 3, raise them again before they clear — a 3-star escape does not count.
A quiet stretch of highway is the best place to lose the tail.

trophies.desc: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.

dispute.a: Yes — the three shops must be robbed in one run with no break. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — the run counts as long as the wanted level never drops between shops. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Rob three shops in one run without stopping; that satisfies both readings.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for robbing 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. Pick three shops on one street, rob them in sequence, and keep the wanted level alive between them — the trick is to keep moving and never let the stars clear. It is flagged at risk because it is a one-run chain: one mistake restarts it.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

steps.t: Wait until a partner mission has your partner with you.
Pick three shops on one street and plan the route.
Rob the first shop, then drive straight to the second.
Rob the second and third without stopping or letting the stars clear.
The trophy pops after the third robbery if the wanted level never dropped.
If the stars clear between shops, start the chain again.
A fast car and a short route are worth more than a big haul.

dispute.a: Yes — only new models count; duplicates do not. [6] [16]
dispute.b: No — any 100 vehicle discoveries count, including repeats. [1] [6]
dispute.call: Drive new models; the counter shows the total as you go.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for discovering 100 vehicles. Every new model you drive for the first time counts — the counter is in Progress > Collections. The fastest route is to sweep the districts: new traffic spawns by district, so a tour of the map with frequent car swaps beats grinding one street.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

steps.t: Open Progress > Collections and see the vehicle count.
Drive a tour of the districts, swapping cars often — new models count, repeats do not.
Check car parks and dealerships for models that never spawn in traffic.
Mark new models in the tracker as you find them.
Keep touring until the counter reads 100.
At 100 the trophy pops.
If the counter stalls, try a new district — traffic spawns by area.

trophies.desc: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.

dispute.a: Yes — all 5 must fall inside one Combat Focus window. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — the count carries across uses as long as the fight never ends. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Take all 5 inside one window; that satisfies both readings.
dispute.q: Must all 5 fall in one window?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for taking down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode — trigger it in a busy firefight, line up five targets, and drop them before the meter runs out. Pick a spot with clustered enemies and a clear line, and do not waste the window on cover.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps.t: Find a firefight with at least five enemies close together.
Take cover and wait until the group is clustered.
Trigger Combat Focus and drop the first target.
Chain the next four without letting the meter run out.
The trophy pops when the fifth falls inside the window.
If the meter runs dry, retreat and try the next fight — the attempt is free.

trophies.desc: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.

dispute.a: Yes — the departure must be by air, from the runway, without a ticket. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — any unscheduled exit from the airport grounds counts. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Leave by air from the runway; that satisfies both readings.
dispute.q: What counts as an unscheduled departure?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for making an unscheduled departure at VCIA. Vice City International Airport: get airside without a ticket and leave by air. The cleanest route is a runway-side vehicle or a stolen plane — get to the runway, get airborne, and the trophy pops on departure.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps.t: Go to VCIA and get airside — a runway-side approach avoids the terminal.
Find a plane or a fast vehicle on the runway.
Get airborne from the runway without a ticket or a flight.
The trophy pops on the unscheduled departure.
If security stops you, try a quieter runway entrance.
A stolen plane is the most reliable way out.

dispute.a: Yes — the Rhino tank run must be done in one sitting. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — the run can be split across sessions. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Do it in one sitting; it is short enough that the question never matters.
dispute.q: Must the Rhino run be done in one sitting?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for the Rhino tank run. Get into a Rhino tank and make it hot — the trophy is about the tank's firepower in a single run. Take it to a busy district, use the cannon, and keep the heat on until the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

steps.t: Find a Rhino tank — the military base and some story beats have them.
Drive it to a busy district.
Use the cannon on targets until the run heats up.
The trophy pops when the run completes.
Keep moving — a parked tank is an easy target.
If the tank is destroyed, steal another and continue the run.

trophies.desc: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.

dispute.a: Yes — the whole robbery must be silent, alarms included. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — only the entry must be undetected; the exit can be loud. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Do the whole job silent; that satisfies both readings.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for robbing a jewelry store without being detected. Pick a quiet hour, enter without tripping the alarm, take the goods, and leave the same way. Silent tools and a slow approach matter more than speed — one alarm restarts the attempt.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

steps.t: Pick a jewelry store and scout it at a quiet hour.
Enter without tripping the alarm or the cameras.
Take the goods quietly and leave the way you came.
The trophy pops when you leave undetected with the goods.
If an alarm trips, leave and try again — the attempt is free.
Night is the best time; fewer staff, fewer witnesses.

dispute.a: Yes — all 5 vaults must be robbed in one crime spree. [9] [16]
dispute.b: No — the 5 vaults can be robbed across any number of sessions. [1] [9]
dispute.call: The counter tracks all 5 either way; rob them one at a time and watch it climb.
dispute.q: Must the 5 vaults be one spree?

trophies.guide: Silver trophy for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping. The vaults are in the five banks across Leonida — each one is a small heist: get in, crack the vault, get out before the response arrives. The counter tracks all five, so work them one at a time with a fast getaway car ready.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

steps.t: Open the bank vault list and note the five banks.
Pick the nearest bank and plan a getaway car first.
Rob the vault and escape before the response arrives.
Mark the vault in the tracker and move to the next bank.
Repeat until all five are robbed.
At 5 the trophy pops.
If an escape fails, the vault still counts once it is cracked — retry the escape.

trophies.desc: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.

dispute.a: Yes — the truck must be robbed on the road, in motion. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — a parked truck counts too. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Hit a moving truck; that satisfies both readings.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for robbing an armored truck and escaping. Armored trucks run set routes through the city — intercept one, stop it, take the cash, and escape before the escort responds. A roadblock or a well-placed ram stops it cleanly.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

steps.t: Find an armored truck on its route through the city.
Intercept it with a roadblock or a ram.
Take the cash from the truck.
Escape before the escort responds.
The trophy pops on a clean escape.
If the escort arrives, lose them first — the cash stays yours.

dispute.a: Yes — every named district must be visited. [1] [3]
dispute.b: No — only the map regions matter, not every district. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Visit every named district; the map shows what is left.
dispute.q: What counts as all of Leonida?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for exploring all of Leonida. Every named district counts — the map tracks them. Tour the state systematically, district by district, and the counter fills in. It pairs naturally with the vehicle and WAiNK sweeps, so do them together.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

steps.t: Open the map and see which districts are still unvisited.
Tour the districts one by one, driving through each.
Combine the tour with the WAiNK and vehicle sweeps.
Mark districts in the tracker as you visit them.
Check the map for any district still grey.
When every district is visited, the trophy pops.
The far districts are the easy ones to forget — end the tour there.

trophies.desc: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.

dispute.a: Yes — one operation per gang, all of them. [10] [16]
dispute.b: No — any operation per gang counts, and some gangs share sites. [1] [10]
dispute.call: Rob one operation for each gang the map names; the tracker shows the gaps.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for robbing an illegal operation belonging to each gang. The gangs run operations across Leonida — the map marks them once you find them. Rob one per gang, quietly if you can, and the trophy pops when the last gang's operation is hit.
trophies.name: Pest Control

steps.t: Open the illegal operation list and note the gangs.
Pick the nearest operation and scout it.
Rob the operation and escape.
Mark the gang in the tracker and move to the next.
Repeat until every gang's operation is robbed.
The trophy pops when the last gang is hit.

trophies.desc: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for enjoying a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Go to the Ocean Beach bar strip at sunset, order a cocktail, and sit where the ocean is in view. It is a quiet trophy — the game counts the moment, not the drink.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

steps.t: Go to Ocean Beach in the late afternoon.
Find a bar on the strip with a sea view.
Order a cocktail and sit where the ocean is visible.
Stay until the moment registers.
The trophy pops when the scene completes.
Sunset is the most reliable time for the view to register.

trophies.desc: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.

dispute.a: Yes — the exit must be through the showroom glass, in a car. [1] [27]
dispute.b: No — any smash-out from the showroom counts. [16] [27]
dispute.call: Drive out through the glass; that satisfies both readings.
dispute.q: What counts as a classic exit?

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for smashing your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive into a showroom, pick a car, and leave through the glass — the trophy is a nod to the series' most famous exit. Any showroom works; the glass is the point.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

steps.t: Pick a vehicle showroom in the city.
Drive in and choose a car.
Smash out through the showroom glass in the car.
The trophy pops on the exit.
If the glass does not break, back up and hit it faster.
Any showroom counts — pick the one with the widest glass front.

trophies.desc: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for the follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go to the alley, bowl a full game, and follow through on every throw — the trophy is about finishing the game, not the score. It pairs with Ten Pin, so do them in the same visit.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

steps.t: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a full game of bowling.
Follow through on every throw until the game ends.
The trophy pops when the game completes.
Stay for a second game if you also want Ten Pin.
Any score counts — finishing is what matters.
The alley is open after the partner unlock.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for a partnership with mass appeal. This one is about the partnership — the two leads working together in front of a crowd. Play a partner mission through to a public moment and the trophy pops. It is one of the cryptic ones: the description gives nothing away, so follow the partner missions and it comes naturally.
trophies.name: Personal Best

steps.t: Play the partner missions in order.
Look for the missions that put both leads in front of a crowd.
Complete the mission's public moment together.
The trophy pops when the moment lands.
If it has not popped, check the partner mission log for an unplayed one.
It cannot be missed — the moment always comes in the partner chain.
Replay the partner missions from the log if needed.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for choices made, for better or worse. Somewhere in the story you make a choice — and the game remembers it. This trophy pops on a story decision, not on a collectible. Play the story and make the call when it comes; either branch counts.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

steps.t: Play the story until a decision point appears.
Make the choice — either branch counts for the trophy.
Finish the mission the choice unlocks.
The trophy pops when the decision resolves.
If no decision has appeared, keep playing — it comes in the later chapters.
The method is unconfirmed across guides, so this guide flags it rather than guessing.
Replay the decision mission from the log if needed.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for second time's the charm. Something in Leonida only works the second time — a retry, a rematch, a second attempt at a thing that failed the first time. The guides do not agree on which attempt it is, so this guide flags it unconfirmed: try the things that failed once, and it pops on the second success.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

steps.t: Note anything that failed on the first attempt — a race, a challenge, a mission.
Retry it a second time.
Succeed on the second attempt.
The trophy pops on the second success.
If it has not popped, try the next failed thing — the trigger is one specific retry.
The method is unconfirmed across guides, so this guide flags it rather than guessing.
Check the activity log for your failed attempts.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for what the hell just happened. Something strange happens in Leonida — an event, a sighting, a moment that makes you stop and stare. The guides do not agree on where it is, so this guide flags it unconfirmed: explore the odd corners of the map, the far beaches and the deep swamps, and it pops when you find it.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

steps.t: Explore the odd corners of Leonida — the far beaches, the deep swamps, the empty roads.
Look for the strange event the guides argue about.
Trigger the event by being there at the right time.
The trophy pops when the event plays out.
If nothing happens, try another odd corner — the trigger is one specific place.
The method is unconfirmed across guides, so this guide flags it rather than guessing.

trophies.desc: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for bowling them over with a melee drive-by. At the bowling alley, take a melee weapon to a drive-by — bowl the pins over with the car, not the ball. It is a joke trophy with a real trick: line the car up with the pins and roll through them.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

steps.t: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley with a car.
Line the car up with the pins.
Drive through the pins with a melee weapon ready — the drive-by is the point.
The trophy pops when the pins go down.
Do it in the same visit as Let's Go Bowling to save a trip.
A slow roll works better than speed — the pins need to fall, not fly.
If the pins will not fall, re-line the car and try again.

trophies.desc: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for earning $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from the big heists; your contacts launder them for a cut. The counter is in Progress > Collections — launder in batches and the total climbs. It pairs with the heist trophies, so the bills come naturally.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

steps.t: Earn Marked Bills from heists and big robberies.
Open the contacts menu and find the laundering contact.
Launder the bills in batches.
Watch the counter in Progress > Collections.
Keep laundering until the total reads $250,000.
The trophy pops at $250,000.
If the contact will not take more, finish another heist for fresh bills.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for spending $100,000 across all shops. Every shop in Leonida counts — clothes, weapons, food, car mods. The counter is in Progress > Collections. The fastest route is car mods: one good car eats the whole total, but spreading it across shops is more fun and just as fast.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

steps.t: Open Progress > Collections and see the spending counter.
Buy clothes, weapons and food across the shops.
Spend on car mods for the biggest single chunks.
Watch the counter climb as you shop.
Keep going until the total reads $100,000.
The trophy pops at $100,000.
If the counter stalls, try a shop type you have not used yet.

trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for purchasing all garage properties. The garages are for sale across Leonida — each one is a property with a price. Buy them all and the trophy pops. The map marks them once you have the money; the expensive ones are the last ones to buy.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

steps.t: Open the property menu and list the garage properties.
Buy the cheapest garages first.
Save for the expensive ones with heist money.
Mark each purchase in the tracker.
Keep buying until every garage is owned.
The trophy pops on the last purchase.
If a garage will not sell, check the money — some need the full price in hand.

trophies.desc: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy for registering 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app lets you register vehicles you own — open it, pick a vehicle, and register it. Ten registrations and the trophy pops. It pairs with the vehicle sweep: register the new models as you discover them.
trophies.name: On the Spot

steps.t: Open the Scooter Bros app on the phone.
Pick a vehicle you own and register it.
Register a second vehicle, then a third.
Keep registering until the counter reads 10.
New models from the vehicle sweep count too.
At 10 the trophy pops.
If a vehicle will not register, check that you own it — rentals do not count.
